sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Nothing on Kasabe prosody. States (p.99) 'we did manage to record a wordlist with Bogon, the last speaker of Kasabe, some several months before his death'; a few Kasabe lexical items appear untone-marked in comparative Tables 1-2 (pp.100-101); p.114 'Of its sister language, Kasabe (Luo), we know even less'. The phonology section (sec. 4) describes Njerep only: 'Njerep has three level tones, High, Mid, and Low' (sec. 4.4, p.106); no mention of stress/accent for either lect.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6 'Kasabe' is purely sociolinguistic/historical (last speaker at Mvurum near Atta died Nov 1995; 'known as Luo to speakers of Njerep'; 'reportedly closely related to Njerep'). Only prosodic remark in the paper is family-historical: Yeni-Kasabe cluster data show former segmental suffixes surviving 'as tonal markers in the better known Mambila dialects'.
